findings.title: CSP style-src 'self' blocks the design's own inline style attributes (table --cols, progress bars)
findings.detail: Build step 13 sets a CSP meta with style-src 'self' while step 7 emits <table class="wide" style="--cols:N"> and the mocks use 53 inline style attributes (bars style="width:0%", margins). HTML style attributes are blocked under that CSP, so --cols would be undefined, wide tables would lose their min-width (D4/D5 degradation) and bars would collapse. Fix: emit no style attributes; use data-cols="N" with CSS table.wide[data-cols="6"]{--cols:6} for 2..10 (or .cols-N classes), utility classes for margins, and JS el.style.width for bars (CSSOM writes are allowed). Keep style-src 'self'.
findings.proof: On every page type at 390 and 1920: document.querySelectorAll('[style]').length === 0 before scripts run; 0 securitypolicyviolation events during the full browser audit; parseFloat(getComputedStyle(table.wide).minWidth) === cols * 13 * rootFontSize for the §3, §12.2 and §15.3 tables.

findings.title: §3 best-10 card title rule returns the venue name for resources 8 and 9; #5 has no italic/quoted span
findings.detail: Build step 10 takes the first *italic* span before a quoted span. In #8 and #9 the first italic span is the journal/venue (*IEEE Robotics and Automation Letters*, *Robotics: Science and Systems XIX*), not the paper title; #5 (ROS 2 Jazzy official tutorials) has neither span. Fix: title = whichever of {first *italic* span, first "..."/“...” quoted span} starts earliest in the cell; else first link text; else whole cell. Test against the fixed list of ten titles (see design-review.md DR-2).
findings.proof: node:test home-data asserts the exact ten titles; crawl check that the ten index.html best-10 card h3 texts start with 'N. <title>' for N = 1..10.

findings.title: <meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark"> contradicts D3 (light first paint regardless of prefers-color-scheme)
findings.detail: Page inventory and mocks/home.html line 6 declare the meta; CSS already sets color-scheme per theme (:root light, [data-theme=dark] dark). The meta lets a dark-preferring UA paint canvas/form controls dark without the stylesheet. Fix: delete the meta; keep per-theme color-scheme in CSS only.
findings.proof: With prefers-color-scheme: dark emulated and empty localStorage, after loading index.html, plan.html and s12.html: document.documentElement.dataset.theme === 'light', getComputedStyle(document.documentElement).colorScheme === 'light', composited html/body background #ffffff.

findings.title: OF-3 and OF-9 acceptance not fully covered by the verification plan
findings.detail: The theme-control audit runs only at 1440 (the button is icon-only below 860 px) and OF-9 (track selector on one row) has no audit. Fix: run the theme audit at 390 and 1440 and add an OF-9 geometry check.
findings.proof: At 390 and 1440 pressing t three times yields aria-label 'Theme: Light. Activate for Dark' -> 'Theme: Dark. Activate for System' -> 'Theme: System. Activate for Light' -> back, html[data-theme] following, icon mode attribute changing, visible label equal to the mode at >=860. OF-9: at 1024/1440/1920/2560 the four .track-group buttons share one getBoundingClientRect().top; at 390/820 exactly two distinct tops with two buttons each.

findings.title: Feed 'Weekly protocol' card adds a row index (1, 2, 3) that §17.1 does not contain
findings.detail: mocks/feed.html numbers the three Normal-week rows 1/2/3 under the header 'Normal week'; the source first cells are 'Normal week', '', ''. D6 forbids numbers the report does not state and the index reads like session numbering. Fix: render the source's own cells (or drop the first column); no added numbers.
findings.proof: Build-time assertion or crawl check: every td text in the protocol card equals a cell string of the §17.1 table in content/roadmap.md.

findings.title: Tracker row-key wording leaves books/media key and the 8-word cap open to two readings
findings.detail: Prose says 'first *italic* span or first link text ... capped at 8 words (books, media)'; the table says books = italic title (col 2), media = first link text. Italic-first for media would collide (two *The Robot Brains Podcast*, two *Sense Think Act* rows). Fix: write the rule once: leading identifier regex ^\*{0,2}([A-Za-z]{0,2}-?\d+)\*{0,2}(?=[.\s(]|$) lowercased; books = first italic span of column 2; media = full text of the first link; '8 words' = first 8 whitespace tokens containing an ASCII alphanumeric, then lowercase, ASCII-fold, [^a-z0-9]+ -> '-', trim.
findings.proof: manifest test asserts the 26 media ids and 14 book ids against a fixture list (including s10:talks:ri-seminar-max-simchowitz-generative-control-action-chunking); collision check fails the build.

findings.title: Two renderer claims are wrong (harmless for this content)
findings.detail: markdown-it 14.1.0's table escapedSplit honours only backslash escapes, not backticks (no table row in the content has a pipe inside a code span, so nothing mangles today); the '94 **[link](url)** cases' figure is 0 (18 links inside bold runs, 32 italic-inside-link). Fix: correct both sentences; add a build assertion that every table row has exactly the header's cell count.
findings.proof: tables test: a fixture row containing `a|b` inside backticks fails the row-arity assertion; the real content passes.

findings.proof: String checks in the crawl: health strip text matches /■ ok \d+ · □ empty \d+ · ✕ failed \d+/; no feed summary ends with '...'; home progress line matches the agreed wording.
